articles.title: I lost the weight on a GLP-1 — and I'm still explaining myself to everyone I love
articles.summary: The most unexpected "side effect" of taking a GLP-1? The judgment. Experts explain why it happens — and how to respond.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

When my doctor suggested I take a GLP-1 for weight loss and to help get my chronic health conditions under control, I expected the usual gauntlet: hours of research on side effects, worry that I'd be a "non-responder," a little queasiness about giving myself a shot. What I didn't expect was how the people closest to me would react to a drug my entire medical team told me to take. A close family member suggested I was taking the "easy way out," despite years of watching me fight medication-induced weight gain — and despite our entire family struggling with the same thing. Another started texting me GLP-1 horror stories, which did nothing but ramp up my anxiety.

It turns out my family's reaction wasn't uncommon — it was predictable, at least to psychologists. They've run versions of the same experiment several times: describe one person, change only how she lost the weight and see who gets judged. The GLP-1 user comes out worse every time. In a 2026 study in the International Journal of Obesity , she was rated lazier and more self-indulgent than a dieter — and people even said they'd be less interested in spending time with her than if she hadn't lost any weight at all. In another study , 402 women who were overweight or had obesity read about a woman who'd lost 15% of her body weight. Participants who were told she'd used a GLP-1 drug reported more dislike than those told she'd dieted and exercised, and were more likely to believe she'd taken a shortcut.

Why do GLP-1 drugs make people so uncomfortable?

People don't usually ask why you take a pill for blood pressure or carry an inhaler for asthma. But a weekly shot for obesity gets filed somewhere else entirely.

"Stigma toward GLP-1 use reflects deeply rooted cultural beliefs about effort, discipline and personal responsibility for weight and health," says Stacy M. Post , a postdoctoral scholar at Georgetown University who conducted the second study. "It's not surprising that GLP-1 drugs are often viewed as a 'quick fix' for a problem that many believe should be solved through willpower and lifestyle changes alone."

Which sets up a trap with no exit. "Our society stigmatizes people for their body size and tells them to lose weight, but when they use an evidence-based medical treatment for weight loss , they may be stigmatized again for not losing weight the 'right' way," says Rebecca Puhl , a professor in the Department of Human Development & Family Sciences at the University of Connecticut.

Why the "easy way out" stereotype doesn't match what obesity experts know

Weight is not a simple "calories in, calories out" equation. There are a lot of factors that determine whether someone can maintain a healthy weight — many of them are completely out of their personal control. "Obesity is a complex, chronic disease driven by biology, genetics, hormones , environment and medications, many of which can promote weight gain or make weight loss difficult," says Dr. Fatima Cody Stanford , an associate professor of medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School.

Because GLP-1 drugs can be highly effective for weight loss , they've picked up an unearned reputation for cheating. "When a treatment is effective, people sometimes assume it must require less effort, which leads to this 'shortcut' narrative," Stanford says.

Researchers put that assumption to the test. Four studies published in Scientific Reports asked 1,205 people across Belgium, the U.S. and the U.K. to read about two men who each lost about 44 pounds over a year. Both changed their diets, both exercised and both were described as "very strict." The only difference: one also took a GLP-1. Participants rated the GLP-1 user as less moral, less competent and less deserving of his success — even though they'd just been told the effort was identical.

GLP-1 medications can cause significant side effects and often involve adjustments to diet, hydration and exercise. "GLP-1s do not replace effort — they make that effort more physiologically achievable," Stanford says. "They are simply one evidence-based tool."

That's reassuring to hear. It's less useful when I'm face-to-face with someone I love who thinks I cheated. What I wanted was a script — or permission to skip the conversation entirely.

Who to tell about your GLP-1 — and who you can skip

"Some individuals choose privacy to avoid stigma, which is understandable given the lingering judgment," Stanford says. "Others choose openness to normalize treatment and reduce stigma over time."

But really, most choose privacy: 69% of current and former GLP-1 users say they're unlikely to tell others they use the medication, according to a recent poll from Virta Health , a metabolic health company. And they're entitled to. "Medication use is personal health information, and it's OK to be selective about whom you tell," Puhl says.

There's a cost to all of us staying quiet, though. "Not disclosing it can send a somewhat deceptive message that significant weight loss is achievable and sustainable through personal lifestyle behaviors," Puhl says. "We know from evidence in the obesity field that this is difficult, and few people sustain substantial weight loss over time."

That's a real tension, and it isn't yours alone to resolve. If you'd rather not get into it when someone compliments your weight loss, "Thank you, I've been working hard" is a complete sentence.

With my family, deflecting wasn't an option — we were going to have the conversation whether I wanted it or not.

What to do when someone judges your GLP-1 use

Before you say anything — or hang up — take a beat.

The comment may not really be about you. "Patients report negative or complicated reactions from loved ones, including skepticism, jealousy or discomfort with change," Stanford says. "These reactions often reflect others' beliefs about weight or their own relationship with it."

Care also has a way of coming across as judgy, so it helps to work out what's actually driving the reaction, Puhl says. "Are they worried about your health? Are they reacting to misinformation they've heard? Do they believe that using medication is somehow morally wrong? Understanding their motivation can help you approach the conversation."

And if you can't tell, ask. A simple "Why do you ask?" puts the ball back in their court.

"When sharing your experiences with using GLP-1s, it may be worthwhile to focus on the health benefits of the medications, rather than just the weight loss outcomes," says Post, who notes doing so "may reduce stigmatizing attitudes."

That extends to the condition itself. "It can be helpful to reframe obesity as a medical condition rather than a personal failing," Stanford says. "Use simple language, such as: 'My body regulates weight differently, and this medication helps correct that.' Emphasizing that obesity involves hormonal and metabolic regulation — not just behavior — can shift the conversation away from blame."

But remember: this is a strategy, not a standard. Nobody should have to prove their reasons are good enough.

Some people won't take the hint. You offer your GLP-1 rundown once, politely and it comes up again at the next dinner — and the one after that. Puhl's advice is to acknowledge the concern once without reopening the subject — then, if it continues, name what will happen next.

That last part is the hard one. It only works if you actually do it.

There's no perfect answer, but here are some lines I've drawn from our experts' recommendations.

"I'm working on my health with my doctor, and I'm keeping the details private."

"I appreciate you asking, but I don't discuss my medications."

"My doctor prescribed it. It's part of my health plan."

"It's helped. It's also been an adjustment."

"I know people have opinions about these drugs. I'm comfortable with mine."

"I understand you have questions or concerns, and I'm happy to talk about those. But this is a health care decision I've made with my doctor that I'm happy with." (This is one Puhl likes to recommend.)

Another Puhl go-to: "I value our relationship, but I'm not willing to have my weight or my medical treatment become a topic of criticism. I'm going to change the subject or end the conversation if this happens again."

"Happy to tell you what it's been like for me, though everyone's different."

You can share more, less or nothing at all, and you can decide fresh every time.

I know the research now. I know the judgment isn't really about me — that it's a script people absorbed long before I filled a prescription. It helps less than you'd think.

"Many people have absorbed the message that weight should be controlled through willpower, discipline and personal effort," Puhl says. "Those cultural beliefs can create shame." No one, she adds, "should feel they have to justify receiving appropriate medical care simply because others disagree with it."

That should be the end of the conversation. But knowing something and believing it are two different things.

Stacy M. Post, PhD, postdoctoral scholar at Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center at Georgetown University

Rebecca Puhl , PhD, Board of Trustees Distinguished Professor in the Department of Human Development and Family Sciences at the University of Connecticut

Fatima Cody Stanford, MD, MPH, MPA , associate professor of medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School

articles.title: 'Frustrated' with childcare, Faridabad woman slits 2-year-old’s throat; arrested
articles.summary: Faridabad mother arrested after allegedly slashing her 2-year-old son’s neck with a paper cutter; child hospitalized, case filed for attempt to murder.
articles.body: GURGAON: A woman allegedly attacked her two-year-old son’s neck with a paper cutter at their home in Faridabad on Wednesday afternoon, seriously injuring the child. The woman was arrested after her husband filed a police complaint, and a case of attempt to murder was registered against her.According to police, the incident took place in the Naveen Nagar police post area on Aug 26. The child’s father, Krishna Kumar, a private company employee and resident of Faridabad’s Shiv Enclave Part-3, told police that he had been married to Kamlesh for around five years and that they have three children.In his complaint, Kumar alleged that Kamlesh often assaulted the children in anger. On Wednesday afternoon, she allegedly assaulted their two-year-old son. When Kumar intervened, she allegedly picked up a paper cutter kept in the house and attacked the boy’s neck.The child suffered serious injuries and was taken to a civil hospital. Despite substantial blood loss, the child was saved after being rushed for timely treatment, police said.Officers from Naveen Nagar police post and Palla police station reached the spot after being informed. Based on Kumar’s complaint, a case was registered at Palla police station under Section 109 of BNS (attempt to murder), and an investigation began.“During the investigation, we learnt that Kamlesh would stay at home with the children while her husband and mother-in-law went to work. She was under stress over the responsibility of looking after the children. Kamlesh, while under mental stress and in anger, picked up the paper cutter and attacked her son on Aug 26,” an investigator said.The Naveen Nagar police post team subsequently arrested Kamlesh from her house. articles.title: Advogado é morto a tiros após ser tirado de imobiliária à força em Campinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo boletim de ocorrência, homem foi ao local para reunião com suposto novo cliente; criminosos chegaram de moto, o arrastaram para a calçada e efetuaram os disparos.
articles.summary: Segundo boletim de ocorrência, homem foi ao local para reunião com suposto novo cliente; criminosos chegaram de moto, o arrastaram para a calçada e efetuaram os disparos.
articles.body:
Um advogado de 45 anos foi assassinado a tiros na noite de quinta-feira (27), em Campinas (SP), após ser tirado à força de dentro de uma imobiliária no Jardim Marisa. O crime aconteceu na Avenida Coronel PM Hélio Barbosa Caldas, no Jardim Marisa.

Câmeras de segurança registraram o momento do crime - veja acima. De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, Rafael Henrique Silva de Mello foi ao estabelecimento para se encontrar com um suposto novo cliente.

Pouco tempo depois da chegada dele, dois homens em uma motocicleta desembarcaram, subiram as escadas da imobiliária e arrastaram a vítima para fora.

Já na calçada, o homem tentou resistir e houve uma breve luta corporal. Em seguida, os dois criminosos atiraram no advogado e fugiram na moto. Uma funcionária da imobiliária presenciou toda a ação.

Advogado é morto a tiros após ser tirado de imobiliária à força em Campinas — Foto: Câmera de segurança

Segundo o registro policial, a vítima chegou à imobiliária em um Hyundai HB20 prata. O veículo estava trancado e foi apreendido para investigação.

A polícia também informou que o celular do advogado foi levado pelos criminosos. O advogado usava um relógio do tipo smartwatch, que também foi apreendido para perícia.

No local, foram recolhidos três projéteis deformados e uma cápsula de calibre .40 S&W.

O caso foi registrado como homicídio no 2º Distrito Policial de Campinas e encaminhado ao Departamento Estadual de Investigações Criminais (DHPP). Até a publicação desta reportagem, nenhum suspeito havia sido identificado ou preso.

O corpo da vítima foi reconhecido pela ex-esposa no Instituto Médico Legal (IML), segundo o boletim.

articles.title: Pró-Pet Mogi das Cruzes: hospital é alvo de queixas após morte de cão | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura divulgou que unidade teria urgência e emergência 24 horas; coordenadora afirma que porta aberta funciona das 7h às 22h e, na madrugada, casos passam por regulação.
articles.summary: Tutores denunciam falhas no Hospital Veterinário Pró-Pet de Mogi das Cruzes após morte de animal e confusão sobre o funcionamento do atendimento de emergência 24 horas.
articles.body:
Hospital Veterinário Municipal Pró-Pet tem fachada e placa de trânsito indicando que funciona 24 horas — Foto: Maiara Barbosa/TV Diário

Anunciado pela Prefeitura de Mogi das Cruzes com atendimento de urgência e emergência 24 horas, o Hospital Veterinário Municipal Pró-Pet é alvo de reclamações de tutores pouco mais de duas semanas após começar a funcionar.

Entre os relatos recebidos pela TV Diário, estão dificuldade para conseguir atendimento, falta de retorno para agendamento e questionamentos sobre o serviço de internação. Em um dos casos, uma cachorra morreu nos braços da tutora pouco depois de deixar a unidade.

Em entrevista ao Diário TV 1ª edição nesta sexta-feira (28), a coordenadora do Núcleo de Bem-Estar Animal (Nubea), Margareth Cunha, afirmou que o hospital funciona com atendimento presencial de porta aberta das 7h às 22h. Entre 22h e 7h, segundo ela, tutores que precisarem de atendimento devem ligar para o telefone 153, que faz a regulação do caso junto ao hospital.

A explicação difere da forma como o serviço foi divulgado inicialmente pela própria Prefeitura. Quando anunciou o início das atividades, em 11 de agosto, a administração municipal informou que “a unidade contará com atendimento de urgência e emergência durante 24 horas por dia”. A fachada também identifica o equipamento como Hospital Veterinário Municipal Pró-Pet 24 Horas.

Além do funcionamento durante a madrugada, tutores procuraram a TV Diário para relatar problemas relacionados ao agendamento e à internação. A coordenadora afirmou que a Prefeitura analisou os casos apresentados pela reportagem e reconheceu dificuldades no sistema de agendamento, mas contestou parte dos relatos.

Kerolyn Souza contou que levou a cachorra ao hospital por volta das 21h30 de 15 de agosto. Segundo a tutora, inicialmente ela foi informada de que o animal não seria atendido.

Kerolyn afirma que, na sequência, a equipe decidiu atender a cachorra. Segundo ela, o animal recebeu medicação para aliviar a dor e soro e, depois, foi liberado. Ao chegar à esquina do hospital, pouco depois de deixar a unidade, a cachorra morreu nos braços da tutora.

Questionada sobre o caso, Margareth afirmou que a Prefeitura fez um levantamento do atendimento e que o animal foi medicado e estabilizado antes de ser liberado. Segundo a coordenadora, a tutora também teria sido orientada a retornar ao hospital caso houvesse piora no quadro.

Margareth classificou a morte como uma “fatalidade” e afirmou que a conduta adotada pelo veterinário foi considerada correta após análise do atendimento.

Questionada se a gravidade do quadro poderia ter exigido internação, a coordenadora disse que a Prefeitura não poderia “ir contra a conduta do médico veterinário que atendeu” e reiterou que, após a verificação do caso, considerou o procedimento adequado.

Tutora de cachorra com câncer relata dificuldade para agendar

Daniele Rozetti afirma que esteve no hospital com a cachorra em 12 de agosto e tentou retornar à unidade no dia 24. Segundo ela, nessa segunda tentativa foi informada de que deveria fazer o agendamento pelo WhatsApp.

A tutora relata que a cachorra tem câncer e que, desde então, tenta conseguir atendimento pelo canal indicado, mas não recebe retorno e não conseguiu marcar consulta ou outro serviço.

Margareth reconheceu que houve dificuldade no sistema de agendamento e atribuiu o problema ao grande número de mensagens recebidas desde a abertura do hospital.

Segundo a coordenadora, em alguns momentos o WhatsApp chegou a receber entre 400 e 500 mensagens em uma hora e chegou a sair do ar por identificar o volume de contatos como possível spam. Ela afirmou que a Prefeitura trabalha para melhorar o fluxo de comunicação.

Ao ser questionada se um animal com câncer deveria ter prioridade, Margareth afirmou que a classificação depende da condição apresentada no momento do atendimento. Segundo ela, os veterinários seguem critérios de urgência e emergência e um animal atropelado, por exemplo, pode ter prioridade sobre um paciente em tratamento contra o câncer.

A coordenadora também afirmou que a demanda aumentou mais de 50% em relação à estrutura anterior e que as equipes trabalham continuamente durante o período de atendimento presencial.

Recepção do Hospital Veterinário Municipal Pró-Pet também tem indicação de 24 horas — Foto: Maiara Barbosa/TV Diário

Prefeitura contesta relato sobre falta de internação

Luana Perleberg contou que procurou atendimento para a cachorra entre os dias 17 e 26 de agosto. Segundo ela, foram feitas tentativas de agendamento pelo WhatsApp sem retorno e houve demora para conseguir atendimento presencial.

A tutora afirma que a cachorra recebeu o diagnóstico de um quadro grave de insuficiência renal e que precisaria ser internada. Segundo Luana, porém, ela foi informada de que a unidade não dispunha do serviço naquele momento e que deveria procurar uma clínica particular.

Margareth contestou essa versão. A coordenadora afirmou que o hospital dispõe de internação e que havia animais internados na unidade.

Segundo ela, após verificar o histórico do atendimento, a orientação dada naquele momento teria sido para que a tutora retornasse posteriormente, e não para que a cachorra fosse internada.

Margareth afirmou ainda que não há orientação para encaminhar pacientes a clínicas particulares, exceto quando o tutor não atende aos critérios socioeconômicos exigidos para utilizar o serviço. Ela pediu que Luana entre em contato pelos canais oficiais para que o caso seja novamente verificado e afirmou que, da forma como o relato chegou à Prefeitura, “não procede”.

Como funciona o atendimento durante a madrugada

Ao anunciar o hospital, a Prefeitura informou que a unidade teria “atendimento de urgência e emergência durante 24 horas por dia, consultórios, centro cirúrgico, internação, salas de procedimentos, exames e uma equipe especializada”.

Antes da abertura, o médico-veterinário Jefferson Leite, da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde e Bem-Estar, também havia afirmado ao Diário TV que a nova unidade ampliaria o horário em relação ao serviço anterior.

“Antes funcionava no horário comercial, agora funciona 24 horas.”

Na ocasião, Jefferson afirmou ainda que animais poderiam ser levados ao hospital durante a noite:

“Durante os finais de semana, por exemplo, ou durante a noite, depois do expediente, nós temos muitos casos de animais atropelados que vão poder ser trazidos para cá e serem tratados então nesse hospital.”

Nesta sexta-feira, Margareth explicou que o atendimento não funciona da mesma forma durante todo o período de 24 horas.

Das 7h às 22h, segundo ela, o hospital funciona com porta aberta e os tutores podem procurar diretamente a unidade. Os casos são atendidos de acordo com a classificação de urgência e emergência.

Das 22h às 7h, aos sábados, domingos e feriados, a orientação é procurar primeiro o serviço de regulação pelo telefone 153. De acordo com a coordenadora, a ligação é transferida para o hospital e um veterinário orienta o tutor sobre como proceder.

articles.title: Vaquejada de Lagarto: Wesley Safadão exalta tradição do evento | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento que reúne competições e apresentações musicais também movimenta vários setores da economia.
articles.summary: A 63ª Vaquejada de Lagarto impulsiona a economia regional e reúne astros como Wesley Safadão na cidade reconhecida como capital nacional do esporte.
articles.body:
A realização da 63ª Vaquejada de Lagarto está movimentando a economia da região e reunindo, desde a última segunda-feira, competidores e artistas que vão se apresentar no evento ou participar diretamente da pega do boi.

Entre eles está Wesley Safadão, que falou com a equipe do SE1 nesta sexta-feira (28), quando se preparava para deixar a cidade. Na noite desta quinta-feira (27) ele participou de um audiovisual de Mano Walter, no Parque de Eventos Zé Rocha.

“A cidade de Lagarto é muito especial, tanto para show como para vaquejada. A gente que gosta do esporte não mede esforços para estar aqui”, disse, antes de embarcar para o Ceará, onde participará de outro evento do gênero.

Wesley Safadão fala sobre participação na Vaquejada de Lagarto — Foto: TV Sergipe

De tradição popular no Nordeste, a vaquejada é reconhecida por lei, desde 2016, como manifestação cultural nacional. A cidade de Lagarto, a 75 km de Aracaju, é oficialmente a capital nacional da vaquejada, conforme publicação do Diário Oficial da União em 2024 .

Em novembro do ano passado os vereadores do município aprovaram a concessão do Título de Cidadão Lagartense para o cantor Wesley Safadão, que é natural de Fortaleza (CE).

Vaquejada de Lagarto — Foto: TV Sergipe/Arquivo

A pista do Aeródromo, localizada perto do Hospital de Amor, registra movimentação intensa com a chegada e a saída de artistas e competidores.

No mesmo local, o cantor Rei Vaqueiro ressaltou a importância do evento “A Vaquejada de Lagarto é tradição. O Brasil inteiro conhece essa vaquejada”, afirmou, destacando que já pretende voltar no próximo ano.

Neste sábado (29), o palco musical do evento será comandado por Patrick Costa, Henrique & Juliano, Henry Freitas e Bia Frazzo.

articles.title: Motociclista e cavalo morrem após acidente em avenida no litoral de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima de 32 anos foi socorrida, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos. Polícia Civil investiga a dinâmica do acidente ocorrido em Guarujá (SP).
articles.summary: Um motociclista e um cavalo morreram após colisão na Avenida Vereador Lydio Martins Corrêa, no litoral de SP; prefeitura alerta sobre perigo de animais soltos.
articles.body:
Motociclista e cavalo morrem após acidente em avenida no litoral de SP — Foto: Reprodução

Um motociclista de 32 anos e um cavalo morreram após um acidente nesta sexta-feira (28), em Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo. O caso aconteceu por volta das 6h, na Avenida Vereador Lydio Martins Corrêa, na altura do bairro Vila Zilda.

Segundo a Secretaria da Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP), guardas municipais encontraram o motociclista caído na avenida e o cavalo morto em outra faixa da via.

A vítima foi socorrida pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e intubada ainda na ambulância, mas morreu antes de chegar ao Hospital Santo Amaro (HSA).

De acordo com a Polícia Militar (PM), uma equipe da Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM) preservou e sinalizou a área. O cavalo permaneceu no local até ser retirado por uma empresa responsável.

O caso foi registrado como homicídio culposo na direção de veículo automotor e prática de abuso a animais no 1º Distrito Policial de Guarujá. Segundo a SSP-SP, a Polícia Civil realiza diligências para esclarecer a dinâmica do acidente.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Guarujá lamentou a morte do motociclista e manifestou solidariedade aos familiares e amigos da vítima. A administração informou que não recebeu denúncias sobre a circulação do animal em via pública antes da batida.

Segundo a prefeitura, a permanência de animais soltos em vias públicas e locais de livre acesso ao público é proibida pelo artigo 194 da Lei Complementar nº 44, que institui o Código de Posturas do município.

A Secretaria de Meio Ambiente e Segurança Climática (Semam) informou que recebe denúncias pelo WhatsApp (13) 3308-7854. Segundo a administração municipal, as ocorrências são averiguadas e, caso o animal seja encontrado, ele pode ser apreendido e o eventual proprietário, responsabilizado.

Ainda de acordo com a prefeitura, as ocorrências envolvendo animais em vias públicas diminuíram neste ano. A administração atribuiu a redução às ações de conscientização da população e à implantação de uma estrutura para recolhimento e acolhimento.

O município informou ainda que conta com baias para acolhimento dos animais, além de serviços de chipagem, vacinação e destinação, equipe especializada e veículos para recolhimento e transporte.

articles.title: Motociclista cai em banheiro químico após acidente em Jundiaí | G1
articles.standfirst: Clayton Lima foi arremessado com a força do impacto da batida e quebrou uma perna. Acidente aconteceu na Rodovia Dom Gabriel, em Jundiaí (SP).
articles.summary: O motociclista Clayton Lima sofreu fraturas na perna após ser arremessado para dentro da cabine transportada por um guincho na Rodovia Dom Gabriel, em Jundiaí.
articles.body:
O motociclista Clayton Lima, de 28 anos, viveu uma situação inusitada na última segunda-feira (24). Ele foi "salvo" de um acidente grave na Rodovia Dom Gabriel Paulino Bueno Couto, em Jundiaí (SP), ao cair dentro de uma cabine de um banheiro químico depois de bater na traseira de um caminhão.

O jovem foi arremessado para dentro de um dos banheiros que era transportado pelo guincho que ele atingiu. Apesar dos perigos da situação, ele sofreu apenas fraturas na perna direita.

Um amigo de Clayton foi socorrê-lo e gravou um vídeo para mostrar a "sorte" do motociclista. Na gravação é possível ver que o caminhão transportava também uma estrutura de ferro, que estava ao lado da entrada da cabine química que Clayton caiu. Veja acima.

Motociclista cai dentro de banheiro químico que era transportado por caminhão — Foto: Alan Santiciolli / Arquivo pessoal

Ao g1 , o motociclista confirmou que, pelo menos, o banheiro estava limpo na hora do acidente. "Lembro de tudo! Da batida até chegar no hospital... Agora está tudo bem, me recuperando graças a Deus" , disse. Já a motocicleta sofreu os maiores danos e, segundo Clayton, não tem mais conserto pois teve perda total.

Após o acidente o jovem foi encaminhado ao Hospital São Vicente, em Jundiaí, onde ficou internado. Nesta quinta-feira (27), ele recebeu alta e pôde voltar para casa.

articles.title: Rafael Greca sofre queda durante ato de campanha e é internado | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-prefeito da capital é candidato a vice-governador na chapa de Sandro Alex. Segundo o partido, queda gerou hematoma e inchaço na perna esquerda do político do MDB.
articles.summary: Ex-prefeito da capital é candidato a vice-governador na chapa de Sandro Alex. Segundo o partido, queda gerou hematoma e inchaço na perna esquerda do político do MDB.
articles.body:
Anúncio foi feito por Rafael Greca, ao lado de Sandro Alex e do governador Ratinho Junior. — Foto: Reprodução

O ex-prefeito de Curitiba, Rafael Greca ( MDB ) foi internado em Curitiba nesta sexta-feira (28). O candidato a vice-governador na chapa de Sandro Alex ( PSD ) sofreu uma queda durante agenda de campanha no município de Maripá.

Segundo respondeu o MDB, a queda provocou um hematoma e inchaço na perna esquerda do candidato, de 70 anos.

O partido afirma que Greca passa bem e apresenta quadro de saúde estável. "Por precaução, cancelou os demais compromissos e retornou a Curitiba, onde foi internado no Hospital Nossa Senhora das Graças para a realização de exames", diz a nota do MDB.

O partido não divulgou informações sobre as circunstâncias da queda.

articles.title: Caminhão carregado com gelo tomba na RJ-106 em Saquarema | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na altura de Rio Seco; motorista saiu ileso e ajudantes foram levados para o Hospital Municipal Porphírio Nunes de Azeredo.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu na altura de Rio Seco; motorista saiu ileso e ajudantes foram levados para o Hospital Municipal Porphírio Nunes de Azeredo.
articles.body:
Caminhão carregado com gelo tomba na RJ-106 em Saquarema — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Um caminhão que transportava gelo tombou na RJ-106, na altura do bairro Rio Seco, em Saquarema , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, nesta quinta-feira (27).

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o motorista não ficou ferido. Já os dois ajudantes que estavam no veículo sofreram ferimentos moderados e foram encaminhados para o Hospital Municipal Porphírio Nunes de Azeredo.

Ainda de acordo com os bombeiros, a pista estava molhada no momento do acidente. O motorista informou aos militares que o caminhão teria apresentado problemas mecânicos antes do tombamento.

Por causa do acidente, o trânsito precisou ser interditado por alguns minutos para o atendimento às vítimas e a remoção do veículo. A circulação na rodovia foi liberada em seguida.

articles.title: 'É um processo longo', diz médico sobre tratamento de lutador de jiu-jitsu que ficou sem movimento das pernas após golpe em competição no Paraná  | G1
articles.standfirst: Willian "Kabuto" Hiroyuki Masuda é faixa-preta, passou por cirurgia e está internado. Competição aconteceu em Londrina e momento foi filmado. Defesa do outro lutador envolvido disse acompanhar o caso.
articles.summary: Willian "Kabuto" Hiroyuki Masuda é faixa-preta, passou por cirurgia e está internado. Competição aconteceu em Londrina e momento foi filmado. Defesa do outro lutador envolvido disse acompanhar o caso.
articles.body:
Em entrevista coletiva concedida nesta sexta-feira (28), o neurocirurgião da equipe médica que atende Willian "Kabuto" Hiroyuki Masuda explicou que o tratamento do atleta "é um processo longo". Atualmente, o lutador está sem o movimento das pernas.

O faixa-preta está internado no Hospital Evangélico, em Londrina , no Norte do Paraná, desde sábado (22), quando lesionou a coluna cervical em uma competição de jiu-jitsu na cidade. Ele estava em uma luta contra Juliano Di Pelli Machado no momento do golpe. Assista acima .

"Ele chegou com uma fratura-luxação de coluna cervical, que é uma situação extremamente grave e o que traz uma compressão da medula e um quadro neurológico bastante grave. Então ele chegou sem movimento do pescoço para baixo e exigiu uma correção rápida dessa luxação para que pudesse estabilizar a coluna e liberar o canal medular e a medula, para que ele possa ter a chance de ter alguma recuperação", disse o médico Marcus Valério Costa.

No dia do golpe, Willian fraturou as vértebras C5 e C6 e passou por uma cirurgia que durou aproximadamente 10 horas. Nesta sexta-feira, ele está acordado, estável, consciente e se alimentando.

Ainda não há um diagnóstico fechado. A equipe médica informou que isso requer tempo.

Na terça-feira (25), familiares e amigos compartilharam um comunicado dizendo que ele apresentava sensibilidade reduzida nos braços . Essa informação foi atualizada na quinta (27), com a notícia de que esses movimentos ficaram mais limitados por conta do inchaço no corpo.

Willian "Kabuto" Hiroyuki Masuda é faixa-preta em jiu-jitsu. — Foto: Redes sociais/Cedida pela organização do evento

Na segunda-feira (24), o promotor Renato de Lima Castro apresentou uma notícia-crime para que o caso seja investigado como lesão corporal de natureza gravíssima.

O g1 teve acesso ao documento, que destaca a diferença de estatura e peso entre os dois atletas (aproximadamente 40 quilos de diferença).

"Ocorre que, em ato de elevada periculosidade, flagrante a qualquer atleta ou espectador comum, o noticiado JULIANO projetou-se completamente, deixando cair todo o seu peso corporal sobre o corpo da vítima Willian ‘Kabuto’, de uma só vez, lesionando severamente a vítima em posição grave de submissão", consta na notícia-crime.

Ao g1 , a Polícia Civil confirmou que irá instaurar inquérito policial para apurar a situação .

O advogado Felipe de Melo, que representa Juliano Di Pelli Machado, disse que um vídeo do atleta tem circulado em redes sociais em que ele fala sobre a situação. Entretanto, segundo a defesa, a gravação foi feita em um canal privado e enquanto ele ainda não sabia sobre a gravidade do caso.

Ele também disse ter solicitado à organização do evento vídeos na íntegra e regras técnicas.

Em nota, a defesa disse que acompanha a investigação e que o lutador está à disposição para prestar esclarecimentos. Leia na íntegra:

"O atleta Juliano Di Pelli Machado, por meio de sua defesa, manifesta-se sobre o ocorrido durante o Campeonato Super Pro Jiu-Jitsu, realizado em Londrina /PR.

Em primeiro lugar, e acima de qualquer outra consideração: Juliano está profundamente abalado com o estado de saúde de Willian Hiroyuki Masuda, atleta a quem respeita e reconhece como adversário de alto nível. Seus pensamentos, e os de sua família, estão inteiramente voltados à recuperação de Willian. À família e à equipe do atleta, Juliano estende sua solidariedade e coloca-se integralmente à disposição para o que estiver ao seu alcance.

Juliano tomou conhecimento, ainda hoje (24), da existência de uma comunicação dirigida à autoridade policial a respeito do episódio. Reafirma seu total respeito às instituições e sua absoluta disposição em colaborar com toda e qualquer apuração, prestando os esclarecimentos que lhe forem solicitados pelas autoridades competentes.

Precisamente por respeito à investigação — e porque a apuração de um fato ocorrido em competição depende de exame técnico do registro audiovisual, do regulamento da modalidade e da manifestação da arbitragem —, a defesa entende que o lugar adequado para os esclarecimentos é o procedimento oficial, e não o debate público. Não se trata de esquiva: trata-se de garantir que os fatos sejam apurados com a serenidade e o rigor técnico que a gravidade da situação exige, e não pela repercussão de imagens editadas em redes sociais.

Juliano é atleta profissional, medalhista em Campeonato Europeu e em Campeonato Mundial, com trajetória construída ao longo de anos de competição em alto nível e sem qualquer histórico de conduta antidesportiva ou punição disciplinar. O jiu-jitsu é sua vida e sua profissão. Os valores da modalidade — respeito ao adversário, disciplina e lealdade — orientam sua conduta dentro e fora do tatame."

O g1 entrou em contato com a Confederação Brasileira de Jiu Jitsu (CBJJ) e questionou se há um posicionamento sobre o caso, mas não houve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Em nota oficial publicada em rede social, o Super Pro Jiu-Jitsu disse acompanhar a situação. Confira:

"Durante o Super Pro Jiu-Jitsu de hoje, um atleta sofreu uma lesão em luta e foi prontamente atendido pela equipe médica e pela ambulância do serviço Mais Saúde, responsável pelo suporte no local. O competidor recebeu os encaminhamentos indicados após a avaliação técnica. A organização acompanha a situação junto à família, prestando o suporte cabível, e reitera seu compromisso com a segurança e o cumprimento de todos os protocolos. Desejamos ao atleta uma pronta recuperação e nos solidarizamos com ele e seus familiares."

O g1 também fez contato com a Federação de Jiu Jistu do Paraná, que explicou que não tinha conhecimento sobre a realização do campeonato.

articles.title: Zelador agredido no DF tem parada cardíaca e quadro volta a ser grave | G1
articles.standfirst: Vanderlei Souza Lima foi agredido por um morador de rua na madrugada de 7 de agosto, na 314 Norte. Médicos investigam possível infecção e devem se reunir com a família na terça.
articles.summary: Após apresentar melhora, o zelador Vanderlei Souza Lima sofreu uma parada cardíaca e segue internado em estado gravíssimo no Hospital de Base, no Distrito Federal.
articles.body:
O zelador de um prédio na Asa Norte, no Distrito Federal, agredido com uma paulada na cabeça por um homem em situação de rua , teve uma parada cardíaca durante a madrugada desta sexta-feira (28) e voltou a apresentar quadro considerado gravíssimo , segundo a família.

Vanderlei Souza Lima , que continua internado na UTI do Hospital de Base, havia apresentado melhora , mas precisou voltar a ser sedado após a parada.

De acordo com Maria Bia, prima do zelador, a equipe médica ainda investiga o que provocou a piora.

Vanderlei tinha sido extubado na sexta-feira passada (21), segundo os familiares, e passou a respirar com auxílio de uma traqueostomia. Ele também vinha reagindo a estímulos durante as visitas.

"Nós estávamos já bem tranquilos porque ele estava apresentando melhora, mas infelizmente, essa madrugada, ele teve essa parada cardíaca e deixou a equipe médica bem preocupada com o estado dele", disse Maria Bia.

Uma reunião entre a equipe médica e os familiares está marcada para a próxima terça-feira (1º). Segundo a prima, os médicos devem atualizar a família sobre o quadro e os resultados das investigações.

Vanderlei Souza Lima foi agredido por um homem em situação de rua. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

O zelador foi agredido com uma paulada na cabeça na madrugada de 7 de agosto, na 314 Norte. Câmeras de segurança registraram uma discussão entre ele e o agressor, que também aparece com uma faca (veja no início da reportagem).

Segundo a polícia, a discussão teria começado depois que o zelador pediu para que o homem saísse das proximidades do prédio.

Zelador e homem em situação de rua discutem antes de agressão no DF — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

O suspeito, identificado como Alexandre da Trindade Leite , de 45 anos, foi preso no dia seguinte ao ataque. Segundo a Polícia Civil, ele já tinha passagens por roubos e furtos.

O caso é investigado pela 5ª Delegacia de Polícia, na área central de Brasília , como tentativa de homicídio. A Justiça havia expedido um mandado de prisão preventiva contra o suspeito.

Zelador agredido com paulada na cabeça segue internado em UTI no DF — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

articles.title: What we know about the 33 British nationals missing in Nepal
articles.summary: Among those reported missing after deadly floods are a 13-year-old girl and 14-year-old boy.
articles.body:
Families are flying out to Nepal to help the ongoing search for 33 British nationals still missing after deadly floods hit the country.

The brother of Neetu Goyal Tiwari , one of the missing Brits who has not been seen since Wednesday, has appealed to officials to locate his sister.

"Please help us find her", Naresh Goyal told the BBC as he struggled to hold back his emotions.

On Friday, Nepalese authorities named 573 tourists who are still missing in the country and despite fears of a second wave of flooding , search efforts have continued.

And as rescue efforts continue in the aftermath of the disaster which killed at least 538 people, details of the missing are slowly emerging.

What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods

Tiwari, 51, had travelled to Nepal to take part in the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra pilgrimage, which was "her dream", her brother Naresh Goyal told the BBC.

She travelled to Delhi from London before heading to Kathmandu on 14 August with a group from the spiritual organisation Isha Foundation.

Tiwari was expected to return to India on Thursday and meet her brother and parents. But now, the family is desperately searching for answers.

"We have called every helpline given by the Indian government and reached out to the British Embassy in Kathmandu as well," Goyal said.

"Please help us find her," he said, his voice breaking. "We are all very scared."

Neetu's husband, Shantanu, added she had been at the Gyirong checkpoint when the floods struck, so the search for her is being coordinated by China.

Anant Patel told BBC Your Voice that he is still waiting for news on his missing parents, Bipin and Mala Patel, who are from Coventry.

The 29-year-old believes his parents - who are also on a pilgrimage - crossed into Tibet from Nepal moments before the the landslide hit the Gyirong border crossing.

He and his brother Deepesh are in touch with the Foreign and Commonwealth Office, and he told the BBC: "It's a difficult situation for us all, and we are doing our best to stay strong as best as we can in the circumstances."

Pramod Poudel, who lives in Uckfield in East Sussex, told the BBC he has not heard from his wife Sumitra Sapkota and family since the flood hit on Wednesday.

"It's a very, very difficult time for me and for my family and my country at this moment, but obviously I have to go and see what's happening there," he said.

Poudel, who goes by the name Pedro, said he is travelling home to Nepal because "my family needs me".

The daughter of Hemangini Patel , 65, said she is still yet to hear from her mother or her aunt Hema Amin , 63.

Patel told BBC Your Voice her mother's last known location is from a TikTok video shared at 06:00 Nepal time, crossing into Tibet.

She said her mother and aunt had been travelling with the Alpine Eco Trek tour when the flooding hit.

"We are trying to get through to British embassy in China but can't even get through," Patel said.

Essex nurse Rajendra Pudasaini said his relatives were "swept away" by the floods.

"My wife's auntie and uncle, and their granddaughter and her husband are missing, and my godson as well," he said.

"They're gone. The speed the water came, they couldn't be saved, they were just swept away."

Tanay Ranjan told the BBC he hasn't heard from his older brother Ankit Ranjan , 39, and sister-in-law Ankita Chandra , 35.

He said he'd last heard from Ankit on 26 August when he had been travelling with tour operator Kailash Journey on a pilgrimage.

The whole group is now missing, Ranjan said, adding: "We don't know if they crossed the border... We don't have a clue where they are. We are very much devastated."

Also missing is Sarada Simkhada , a senior nurse at Darent Valley Hospital in Kent.

Her brother Shambhu said that her family was desperately waiting for news of her safety after she lost contact with her relatives while on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash.

"My dear sister, wherever you are, please stay strong. We are praying for your safety every moment and waiting desperately for you to return home," he wrote on social media.

A family of four, including an 18-year-old A-Level student and a 13-year-old girl, from Surrey are also among the missing.

Spandan Sahu , 18, was in Nepal with his father Santosh Sahu , 46, his mother Surabhi Manmath Padhy , 44, and sister Syna Kumari Sahu , 13.

In a statement, a spokesperson for the school said: "It is with great concern that we have been informed that a former student, along with members of his family, have been reported missing in Nepal.

"Whilst we are hoping for positive news, we do not have any further information at this time.

"Our thoughts, love and deepest sympathies are with all of the families and loved ones of anyone affected by this tragedy in Nepal at this incredibly difficult time."

Vikram Kolagatla, from London, told the BBC he has not heard from his wife, Geetha Reddy, since the flooding hit.

Reddy, who has two daughters aged 12 and 14, had been in Hotel Kailash in Rasuwagadh when the flooding hit.

"We're not sure what to do. I have two little girls, and their schools are starting next week," Kolagatla added.

"The kids still don't believe it. They think she's stuck in the flood and that she'll come back. They think she's stuck somewhere and there's no mobile network."

Tatajana Phillips , from Folkestone in Kent, told the BBC she has not been able to contact her sister who was near the Nepal-Tibet border when devastating flash flooding hit.

She said the last known location of her sister Julija Jakovicka was in the border area an hour before the flash floods struck.

"Then there is no more news," she told the BBC.

Phillips said her sister, a mother-of-two living in Germany, was in the country for a yoga and meditation retreat.

"We are terribly worried," added Phillips' husband Ben. "We just know where they were and that's really tough."

Her husband, Bhupesh Bector, told The Times: "I know that she's in Nepal for sure, so even if they find her today or tomorrow, I need to be there."

University of Kent graduate Nabhi Das from Streatham in South London has also been widely reported as missing Nepal.

A British psychiatrist is also among the missing.

Pravin Atmakur , 54, was leading a group of 77 pilgrims in Tibet when the floods hit, the Telegraph reports.

His wife, Manjula Atmakur, has travelled to Nepal to help look for him.

She said she felt let down by the British government's response to the flooding .

Several of those missing had been making a pilgrimage to the sacred Hindu site of Mount Kailash, Nepalese tour operator The Trekkers' Society said.

The operator said nine British nationals on one of its tours to the site were among those unaccounted for, including four males, aged 14, 50, 50 and 54, and five females, aged 40, 46, 50, 50 and 53.

Tour companies including Alpine Eco Trek, The Trekkers' Society, Himalayan Glacier US, Kailash Journeys and Fishtail Tours have reported missing British nationals while on trips with the companies.

Alpine Eco Trek said it has not been able to establish contact with 12 Britons who were booked on a tour to Mount Kailash and were in the region when the flash floods struck.

The company's travel logs which were shared with PA Media.

Four of the firm's Nepali tour guides are also missing.

The flood hit early on Wednesday in Rasuwa, just north of Nepal's capital Kathmandu.

Preliminary information suggested it was caused by an earthquake, but the US Geological Survey said additional analysis indicated "the seismic energy was instead generated by a landslide."

It said a magnitude 5.2 seismic event caused by a "glacial collapse and debris flow" occurred near the border at 08:37 local time (03:52GMT) on Wednesday.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK has offered £5m to help the Nepalese government following the floods, saying it was a "very distressing and devastating situation".

He had previously urged Britons in the region "to follow guidance from the local authorities and follow our travel advice".

Speaking on Thursday, King Charles said he and the Queen were "heartbroken" and sent their "most profound sympathy" to those affected.

Watch: What caused the Nepal-Tibet flash floods?

'The flood took everything': Nepal survivors describe horror of loved ones being swept away

Collapsed glacier likely caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, scientists say

articles.title: Baby died after Royal London Hospital monitor volume was too low
articles.summary: The coroner urged the manufacturer of alarms used at the Royal London Hospital to change the volume options.
articles.body:
A coroner has raised concerns after a boy died following a medical emergency that went unnoticed because a hospital monitor alarm was set too low.

Ismaeel Islam, who was under six months old, died at the Royal London Hospital's special care baby unit on 7 March 2025.

Coroner Mary Hassell said he suffered a desaturation and respiratory arrest on 3 November 2024 which went unnoticed for about 30 minutes because the alarm's volume had been turned "too low to be usefully audible".

The coroner found this medical emergency led to his death. She issued a Prevention of Future Deaths report to Masimo UK, the maker of the monitoring alarms used at the hospital. Masimo UK has 56 days to respond.

Hassell, who led an inquest into the death at North London Coroner's Court, said the nurse caring for Ismaeel, who had health problems linked to Down's syndrome, growth restriction and prematurity, was attending to another baby at the time and he was not in her line of sight.

The coroner acknowledged that Barts Health NHS Trust, which runs the hospital, had since introduced measures to improve the audibility of alarms and lines of sight to cots on the unit.

However, she raised concerns that the alarms could be set at a volume too low to be heard and said there was a risk of future deaths unless action was taken.

She has called for baby monitors to be locked at a maximum volume or set to maximum.

"If Ismaeel's deterioration had been recognised immediately and treated appropriately, his life would have been saved," she said in her report.

Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook , X and Instagram . Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk

articles.title: ‘Where’s the humanity?’: Imran Khan’s sons fear for jailed ex-Pakistan PM
articles.summary: Sulaiman and Kasim Khan are increasingly worried after hearing their father is ‘agitated’ and suffering from anxiety.
articles.body:
London, United Kingdom – Sulaiman and Kasim Khan have not heard their father’s voice in almost six months.

The last time they spoke to Imran Khan, the imprisoned former prime minister of Pakistan and cricket legend, was over Eid al-Fitr in March. The call lasted 20 minutes.

“We don’t know how much time we have to speak,” Kasim, 27, told Al Jazeera in London. “Usually it’s around the 20-minute mark. He frantically asks about our lives and gives us advice. But when we ask about him, he very quickly shuts it down. He doesn’t seem to want to talk too much about how he is.

“You know, it is what it is,” Kasim recalled him saying.

Three years have passed since Khan, 73, was imprisoned in Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail. He has faced more than 100 legal cases since his 2022 ouster in a vote of no confidence, including charges of bribery, leaking state secrets and illegally selling state gifts. He denies all of the accusations against him.

All of his convictions but one have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending.

Khan’s family and his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party believe the charges are politically motivated.

Two of his sisters, Uzma and Noreen, were recently allowed to see him. They said it was the first visit they had had in months.

“They were both quite disturbed by how agitated he was. He’s been mentally tortured with this solitary confinement ,” Sulaiman, 29, said.

“His heart rate spikes considerably in his cell. He’s having palpitations due to severe anxiety,” said Kasim. “He’s the most calm, mentally strong person I’ve ever known by a considerable margin. To hear he’s facing anxiety, it’s unfathomable.”

Khan’s lawyers reported in February that he had lost 85 percent of the vision in his right eye.

“He was still wearing an eye patch when he saw our aunt the other day,” Sulaiman said. “For 10 months he wasn’t allowed any visitors. Apart from that brief visit from his sisters, none of the other orders have been followed.”

Pakistan’s Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, in a statement sent to Al Jazeera, rejected the family’s allegations , that Khan has been denied appropriate medical care “or that the government failed to comply with the directions of the Honourable Supreme Court regarding his medical examination”.

“Health matters” should not be politicised, the statement continued, adding that the government “has never adopted a disrespectful attitude towards anyone’s health”.

On August 18, a three-judge Supreme Court bench ruled that Khan be moved to the private Shifa International Hospital within two days, that he be granted weekly family visits and twice-weekly calls with his sons, and ordered that his personal physician and sister, both doctors, be allowed to take part in his medical care. Earlier, a cardiac board review found Khan had fluctuating blood pressure and anxiety, attributed to limited contact with his family.

But he was instead taken to a government hospital, PIMS, for a brief check-up before returning to jail on August 20. Khan’s party has since filed a contempt petition.

“These government doctors are essentially told what to say,” said Sulaiman. “We want him independently checked, so we have proof. What are they hiding?”

“The establishment currently has absolute power. Any efforts by the Supreme Court seem ineffective,” said Kasim. “We’re just trying to make as much noise as possible.”

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said reports of Khan’s ill health were “not supported by prison or medical records”.

It said Khan has undergone 30 medical examinations since his imprisonment began “in addition to regular examinations by the prison doctor” and that doctors had recently concluded that he appears “oriented, stable and without any recorded acute or unmanaged deterioration”.

Support for Khan’s release has come from the United Nations, Amnesty International, politicians in Washington and London, and 21 former cricket captains .

“We’re hoping the UK could make a difference,” said Kasim. “Our father lived here a long time, and he’s always spoken very highly of England.”

Their mother, Khan’s ex-wife Jemima Goldsmith, has called on Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband for help, saying Khan has “endured three years of solitary confinement” in what has become a “human rights emergency”.

She said that their sons, who are British citizens, have been denied visas and warned they risked arrest if they travelled to see Khan, calling the situation “a human-rights emergency.”

Khan’s sons last met him in November 2022 after an attempted assassination on his life.

“We have plans, but we can’t disclose exactly what they are, because anything we say publicly is often very quickly intercepted by those in Pakistan,” Kasim said.

“Now is the toughest time, the bleakest it’s looked. But at least there’s more attention now,” Sulaiman added. “We’re lucky to have good friends and a strong family unit who keep us sane.”

The Pakistani ministry also denied claims that Khan has been isolated or denied contact, saying, “Records show approximately 198 interview sessions involving more than 900 visitor entries. These include his sisters, family members, lawyers, doctors, political representatives and other approved visitors.”

It described his prison conditions as humane, saying the facilities allow for “sleeping, sanitation and exercise”.

“He receives separately prepared meals, including meat, chicken, fruit, milk, nuts, juices and bottled water,” it said. “At the same time, access to a prisoner cannot be used as a platform for unrestricted political communication or political activity from inside prison.”

Khan had kept his sons out of the limelight and neither sought a life in front of the cameras.

Kasim said he holds the government responsible for their father’s deteriorating health.

“Where is the humanity in not allowing someone to receive basic health checks or treatment? It’s the pettiness, the petty torture techniques, not allowing him to have books, phone calls with his children, keeping him for 23 hours in an isolated cell,” he asks.

“If they reject any claims of mistreatment, prove it. Bring him to an unbiased doctor and hospital, and show the medical reports. It puts our minds at ease, and shows the people of Pakistan that their elected leader is healthy.”

But he continues to believe in his father’s strength.

“If there’s hope that anyone can remain resilient through this period, it’s him, even though it’s so brutal in these conditions,” said the younger brother.

articles.title: Measles deaths may have been 'fabricated,' RFK Jr claims after coroner raises questions
articles.summary: RFK Jr. alleged Pennsylvania's two measles-associated deaths may have been "fabricated" as a dispute with Gov. Josh Shapiro over the outbreak intensifies.
articles.body: Days after Pennsylvania health officials reported two measles deaths, a public dispute has emerged about whether other factors played a role in the fatalities. The Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) confirmed the two "measles-associated" deaths on Tuesday, noting that both individuals were unvaccinated. These were the state’s first measles-related deaths in 35 years, according to the release. FORMER CDC ADVISOR SAYS DECLINE IN KINDERGARTEN VACCINATIONS NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT: 'KEEP CALM AND CARRY ON' That confirmation came after the county coroner — physician Stephen Diamantoni — said the newborn died shortly after birth from a lacerated spleen and had tested positive for measles acquired before birth, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer. Diamantoni’s office was still investigating the newborn’s death, and the coroner said he was not aware of the other reported death, Axios reported. The Pennsylvania Department of Health stated that not all deaths are referred to a coroner under state law. The DOH says it uses the term "measles-associated" when laboratory or epidemiologic evidence of measles is present, even if a coroner or medical certifier does not identify measles as the immediate cause of death. Measles can affect the spleen, potentially causing enlargement and, in rare cases, rupture, according to Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst. Pregnant women, newborns and young infants can face a higher risk of serious measles complications, the doctor noted. Infants who are too young to receive the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine can be especially vulnerable. COMMON VACCINE LINKED TO 24% LOWER DEMENTIA RISK IN OLDER ADULTS HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has questioned whether Pennsylvania officials provided sufficient information to substantiate the two measles-associated deaths. In a Wednesday post on X, after the coroner’s comments were made public, Kennedy alleged that Pennsylvania had not given the CDC relevant information and suggested the deaths could have been "fabricated." "The announcement appears to have been premature, and the deaths may even have been altogether fabricated by one of the Governor's hopeful staffers," he wrote. "The Lancaster County Coroner says that it has no record of any measles deaths." RFK also accused Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro and his office of "fearmongering, misinformation, finger-pointing and the weaponization of infectious disease fears for political gain." "The Lancaster County Coroner says that it has no record of any measles deaths." Meanwhile, at a Tuesday press conference, Shapiro said the deaths showed the "real-life consequences" of misinformation about the measles vaccine. In a subsequent X post, the governor claimed Kennedy had "stoked confusion amongst parents and others — and the result has been less protection from measles and more cases." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES In response to Kennedy’s comments, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention also spoke on X about the debate, expressing appreciation for RFK’s efforts to "clarify conflicting information" about the cause of the two reported deaths. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "CDC is working to determine what actually occurred," the agency wrote. "These discrepancies raise important questions, particularly because the Governor’s Office has not provided CDC with information relevant to the outbreak and has declined our offers of assistance." "Under President Trump’s and Secretary Kennedy’s leadership, CDC will follow the facts and tell the American people the truth." Pennsylvania Health Secretary Dr. Debra Bogen disputed the CDC’s account, saying the two deaths were reported to the agency’s measles response team early Tuesday morning. In an X post from the Pennsylvania Department of Health account, Bogen said she had reviewed the case investigations and that state epidemiologists had thoroughly investigated both deaths. She confirmed that both individuals tested positive for measles. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Meanwhile, Lancaster County Commissioner Josh Parsons said he did not believe there was enough evidence to confirm the two deaths were caused by measles, citing information he said he received from the county coroner’s office, according to Local21 News. What does ‘measles-associated’ mean? Siegel noted that measles weakens the immune system and increases the risk of pneumonia, which can stem from measles itself or from a secondary bacterial infection. "If the impact of measles on the immune system or stress on other major organs as a result of the disease leads to death, that would be a measles-associated death," he told Fox News Digital. When a patient has both measles and another immediate cause of death, several considerations come into play when infectious disease specialists are determining whether the virus was a contributing factor. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It has to do with whether the immediate cause of death is from measles itself, as in measles pneumonia, or due to damage to the immune system and secondary infections or other diseases that result," Siegel said. Lancaster County is at the center of Pennsylvania’s current measles outbreak. As of Friday, the state had reported 424 confirmed cases and 73 hospitalizations. Fox News Digital reached out to the involved government officials requesting comment.

articles.title: Canada poaches dozens of top US researchers for its universities
articles.summary: Researchers in fields like climate and medicine are being lured north by new research funding.
articles.body:
Canada is hiring dozens of researchers away from US universities, including top research institutions such as Harvard as its relationship with its neighbour continues to sour.

More than three-fourths of the 64 professors who are moving to Canada from around the world will come from the US. Under a new government programme, they'll receive funding from a pool of C$504m ($362m; £268m) for research in fields such as climate change and medicine.

US President Donald Trump's administration has accused universities of being dominated by left-wing ideology and diversity policies, and of failing to tackle alleged campus antisemitism.

The BBC contacted the White House and US Department of Education.

The administration has also frozen federal research grants for many different institutions and groups that they have argued are wasteful . That uncertainty is helping lure researchers elsewhere.

Meanwhile, Canada is asserting itself more on the global stage while it pushes back against the US in their escalating trade war, which reached a major turning point over tariffs recently .

One climate researcher told the BBC he was relocating to Canada in part because his work in the US had become more difficult in recent years.

Seth Guikema, a climate resiliency researcher at the University of Michigan and one of the 48 US researchers relocating to Canada, said he decided to approach Canadian institutions last year in search of opportunities.

"The funding environment in the US for anything related to climate and resilience has become challenging," Guikema said. "I was looking for a good intellectual home where I could have practical impact."

Over the next eight years, Guikema said he would use C$8m to research tools for better preparing for natural hazards, like storms and wildfires, at the University of Western Ontario.

The University of Michigan, his former employer, declined to comment.

Canada's Industry Minister Melanie Joly said on Thursday the government was "very glad that these fantastic professors are coming".

Asked if the programme was poaching US talent and whether it could be viewed by the Trump administration as an escalation of the US-Canada trade war, she said on Thursday: "The US administration is taking its own decisions and we're taking ours."

Some of the researchers chosen for the programme, like Guikema, were born and raised in the US. Others are Canadians who worked abroad and are now returning home.

Peter Caravan, who worked for two decades as a biopharmaceutical researcher and professor at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School, appeared emotional at a Thursday news conference announcing the research appointments.

Caravan is researching how illnesses like cancers and chronic diseases can be better detected - work that will now be done out of the University of British Columbia in Vancouver.

Steven Lamy, a professor of International Relations at the University of Southern California, argued that major grant agencies "have been cut and politicised" by the current US administration.

"All of a sudden employment offers from external universities are attractive," he said.

Stephanie Burt, an English professor at Harvard University, believed the funding cuts were "a generational disaster for science and scientists".

She told the BBC that Canada had offered a "far more welcoming environment" for academics.

US universities are still among the top ranked in the world, according to QS Universities Rankings, with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Stanford and Harvard in the top five.

Lynn Pasquerella, the president of the American Association of Colleges and Universities, said institutions feel "helpless" in the face of federal and state cuts.

The deeper concern, she added, "is not the short-term brain drain", but "the possibility that the US could become less attractive as a place to pursue knowledge".
